html:
The Bogotazo was a huge riot in Bogotá on 9 April 1948, after the murder of the Liberal leader Jorge Eliécer Gaitán. Much of the city centre was burned, and hundreds, perhaps thousands, died.

Gaitán was a popular orator who attacked the oligarchy of both parties, and many expected him to win the presidency. He was shot outside his office at lunchtime. A crowd killed his assassin, then looted and burned churches, offices and shops, and the police split. A pan-American conference was meeting in Bogotá at the time; it founded the Organization of American States. A young Fidel Castro was in the city as a student delegate.

The riot spread to other towns. It deepened the hatred between Liberals and Conservatives and opened the bloodiest years of La Violencia, which later fed the guerrilla wars of Colombia.
sum: The Bogotazo was a huge riot in Bogotá on 9 April 1948, after the murder of the Liberal leader Jorge Eliécer Gaitán. Much of the city centre was burned, and hundreds, perhaps thousands, died.
